title: Three Products and a Fourth
statement:
Real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy
$$(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=5,\qquad (a+2)(b+2)(c+2)=-3,\qquad (a+3)(b+3)(c+3)=4.$$
Find the value of $abc$.
hints: Don't try to find $a$, $b$ and $c$ individually. Look at the single function $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$. The three conditions give its values at $x=1,2,3$, and $abc$ is its value at $x=0$.

Use finite differences on the values of $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$ at $x=0,1,2,3$. This polynomial is a cubic with leading coefficient $1$, and the third difference of such a cubic is the same constant whatever its other coefficients are.

Write $F(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ and check the combination $F(3)-3F(2)+3F(1)-F(0)$ term by term: the terms in $p$, $q$ and $r$ all cancel, and the $x^3$ terms leave $27-3\cdot 8+3\cdot 1-0=6$. Now put in the known values of $F(1)$, $F(2)$ and $F(3)$.
solution: Let $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$. The given conditions say that $F(1)=5$, $F(2)=-3$ and $F(3)=4$, and we want $F(0)=abc$. Expanding shows that $F(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ for some real numbers $p$, $q$ and $r$. Taking the third difference of $F$ means forming the combination $F(3)-3F(2)+3F(1)-F(0)$, and we can work it out one power of $x$ at a time. The $x^3$ terms give $27-3\cdot 8+3\cdot 1-0=6$. The $px^2$ terms give $p\,(9-3\cdot 4+3\cdot 1-0)=0$. The $qx$ terms give $q\,(3-3\cdot 2+3\cdot 1-0)=0$. The constant terms give $r\,(1-3+3-1)=0$. Hence $$F(3)-3F(2)+3F(1)-F(0)=6,$$ whatever the values of $p$, $q$ and $r$. Substituting the known values gives $4-3\cdot(-3)+3\cdot 5-F(0)=6$, that is, $28-F(0)=6$. So $F(0)=22$, and therefore $abc=22$. Why this works. finite-differences, factored-form-of-polynomial: reading the product as a monic cubic in factored form gives values at four consecutive integers, and the third difference eliminates all the unknown coefficients at once.
